clue.text: Unhappy, being left to open French and Spanish wines

indicators.note: the letter for left goes in to open up the French wine name, sitting inside it

parts.note: Macon is a French wine from Burgundy
tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A gloomy drinker grumbles, having been abandoned to uncork bottles of French and Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French and Spanish wines' reads as one list, but 'French' alone is MACON and 'Spanish wines' alone is TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A discontented person, or as an adjective someone dissatisfied with things, is unhappy.

clue.text: Live entertainment thus gets a bit of a laugh in Scottish island

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these pieces go inside the island name

parts.note: Mull is an island of the Inner Hebrides
sic is Latin for thus
ha is one syllable of laughter, ha-ha

explanation.surface: Live shows on a Scottish island raise a laugh or two.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre staging variety shows, and the variety entertainment itself, performed live.

clue.text: Using dictionary, checks graffitist's spelling of "school"?

definitions.text: Using dictionary, checks graffitist's spelling of "school"?

parts.words: Using dictionary, checks graffitist's spelling of "school"?
parts.note: consults a reference book; and a graffiti writer spells school as skool, which written upward in a down entry reads the other way

explanation.walkthrough: Graffiti spells school SKOOL; written upwards in this down light it reads LOOKS, with UP saying how.
explanation.definitionFit: To consult a dictionary or other reference for a word or fact.

clue.text: Perhaps a Crufts winner fails to finish piece of meat

indicators.note: fails to finish means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a champion gundog at Crufts might be the number one setter, written NO I SETTER

explanation.surface: A dog-show champion fails to finish a piece of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's big dog show; 'No 1 setter' gives NOISETTER, and 'fails to finish' drops its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round boneless cut of lamb or other meat.

clue.text: Instrument out of tune in Elgar concerto

indicators.note: playing out of tune is wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instrument plays out of tune during an Elgar concerto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of tune' rearranges IN ELGAR CONCERTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument making organ sounds electronically, a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Sound quality of broadcast about preserving old railway

indicators.note: preserving means keeping inside, so the railway letters go within
about means turned round, so the broadcast word is read backwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out or broadcast
BR is British Rail, the former national railway

explanation.surface: A broadcast about saving an old railway has fine sound quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EMIT into TIME, which keeps BR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive tone or character of a voice or instrument's sound.

clue.text: Mark time after retiring? Terrific

indicators.note: the reversed time is placed after the mark letter

parts.note: M stands for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for time is read backwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether marking time after retirement could be terrific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns AGE into EGA, which follows M.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang adjective meaning great or excellent, a close synonym of terrific.

clue.text: Moving display given by actor performing in style

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the rearranged letters go inside the style word

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on an act, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An actor performs in style for a moving show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges ACTOR as TORCA, inside MODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession of cars, a display that moves along a route.

clue.text: In speech shopkeeper is more vulgar

indicators.note: in speech means spoken out, so a word sounding like this is spelt differently

parts.note: a grocer is a shopkeeper selling food

explanation.surface: In talking, a shopkeeper is coarser than others.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of gross, meaning coarse or crude.

clue.text: Nine owls flying about where it's high and cold

indicators.note: birds flying about move freely, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Nine owls flit around a cold mountain height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying about' rearranges NINE OWLS.
explanation.definitionFit: The altitude above which snow lies all year, found on high cold mountains.

clue.text: Brisk pace mostly adopted by staff nurse

indicators.note: taken in by, so the shortened pace goes inside the staffing word

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter of the word for brisk pace is dropped

parts.note: a trot is a brisk pace

explanation.surface: A hospital's staff nurse takes on a brisk walking pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TROT to TRO, which sits inside MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior nurse in charge of a ward or of nursing in a hospital.

clue.text: Detective work: hunt down missing husband

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for husband is taken away

parts.note: to chase is to hunt down

explanation.surface: A detective's job: tracking down a husband who has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops H from CHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under investigation by a detective is called a case.

clue.text: Present award, say, for business initiative

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is heard rather than read, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: to enter is to present or submit, and a prize is an award

explanation.surface: A prize is presented for business initiative.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprise means resourcefulness and initiative, especially in starting business ventures.

clue.text: Hand out a soft drink about middle of afternoon

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the drink goes round the central letter

parts.note: a potion is a drink, often medicinal or magical

indicators.note: the central letter of the ninth-letter word afternoon is taken

explanation.surface: Someone distributes a soft drink at around mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft drink' looks like one item, but 'soft' is P and 'drink' POTION; 'about' wraps POTION round R, the middle letter of 'afternoon'.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion is to share or distribute among people, to hand out.

clue.text: Photo sent for development immediately

indicators.note: development of film changes it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A photo sent off to be developed straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for development' rearranges PHOTO SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning at once, without delay, right there.

clue.text: Duos rendering songs with power

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
airs are tunes or songs

explanation.surface: Duets are performing songs powerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Duos and pairs are both sets of two.

clue.text: Writer still cherished among foremost of Scotland's top novelists

indicators.note: held lovingly within, so the phrase for still goes inside the initial letters
the first letters of the three words are taken

parts.note: even so means nevertheless, still

explanation.surface: A writer still loved among Scotland's leading novelists.
explanation.walkthrough: S, T, N, the initials, hold EVEN SO between T and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish author, of Treasure Island fame.

clue.text: Combat ruin, getting in right mess here?

parts.note: war is combat

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the right letter goes inside the ruin word

parts.note: doom is ruin

explanation.surface: Fighting brings ruin, so put things right in this mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' is not a muddle but where naval officers eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The officers' dining room on a warship, a place where they eat together.

clue.text: Port should be kept in bottle, I think

indicators.note: the letters are kept inside the run of words, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Someone thinks port ought to be stored in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink, but it is a harbour town; it lies in bottLE I THink.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is the port district of Edinburgh in Scotland, on the Firth of Forth.

clue.text: English novelist, man of letters for the modern age?

definitions.text: man of letters for the modern age?

parts.note: Norman Mailer was an American novelist

explanation.surface: An English novelist is a modern man of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sending electronic messages, a whimsical modern writer of letters.

clue.text: Stuck in marshy ground, Magwitch wants large drink

indicators.note: something stuck in is placed inside, so the convict's first name and the large letter go inside the marshy word

parts.note: mire is boggy, marshy ground
Abel Magwitch is the convict in Dickens's Great Expectations

explanation.surface: Dickens's convict, bogged down in the marshes, longs for a big drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Magwitch first appears on the Kent marshes, hence the apt surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless brandy distilled from small yellow plums, so a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Leader struggles to contain western islands

indicators.note: to contain means to hold inside, so the western letter goes within
struggles suggests thrashing about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leader struggles to hold the western islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' rearranges LEADER, which takes W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a Caribbean chain in the Lesser Antilles.

clue.text: In school clear up nasty smell

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the reversed piece goes inside the school abbreviation
up in a down clue means read from the bottom, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to net is to clear as profit

explanation.surface: Clearing up at school releases a horrid smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NET into TEN, inside SCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, offensive odour.

clue.text: Mother and father are in such a state

definitions.text: Mother and father are in such a state

parts.words: Mother and father are in such a state
parts.note: a mother and a father share the condition of having children, which is what the clue describes

explanation.definitionFit: The state or condition of being a mother or a father to a child.

clue.text: Shoe tree oddly unsuitable as present

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are unwanted, so only the even-placed letters remain

explanation.surface: A shoe tree turns out strangely unsuitable as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in this place means being in attendance, a synonym of present.

clue.text: Type of garment one shortened by mistake

parts.note: a slip is a small error or mistake

indicators.note: shortened means cut, so the word one loses its final letter

explanation.surface: One garment was shortened by an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' turns ONE into ON, which goes beside SLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes clothing or shoes pulled easily on without fastenings.

clue.text: Containers of compost gardener initially obtains on line

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so obtains comes after line
the first letter of the word gardener is taken

parts.note: a row is a line of things
to bag something is to obtain it

explanation.surface: A gardener first gets compost bags on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic sacks filled with compost, in which plants such as tomatoes are grown.

clue.text: Our last king's appeal for courage and determination

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of King George VI, Britain's last king
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Britain's most recent monarch called for bravery and resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is an old crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit means strength of character, pluck and resolve.

clue.text: Servant's to offer help feeding people

parts.note: to hand something is to give or offer it

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so the help word is put inside the people word

parts.note: men are people
aid is help

explanation.surface: A servant has to provide help in feeding people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Servant's' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A female attendant or maid, an old word for a servant.
